title: Hexagram 1 – Qian (乾) – The Creative, Heaven
body_md:
Qian is six yang lines stacked together: the image of heaven moving without pause. The judgment speaks of great, originating success on condition of remaining firm and correct. The image teaches the noble person to model heaven and strengthen themselves without rest.

When you cast Qian, you are in a season of strong creative force and will; anything can be started, provided it is started rightly. The thing to watch is arrogance: the dragon that flies too high has cause for regret. This week, choose one worthy goal and work on it steadily every day with nobody watching.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 2 – Kun (坤) – The Receptive, Earth
body_md:
Kun is six yin lines: the image of the wide earth carrying all things. The judgment speaks of success through the steady virtue of a mare; if the noble person takes the lead they go astray, if they follow they find their lord. The image teaches supporting people and things with large virtue.

When you cast Kun, you are reminded that strength now lies in receiving, yielding and nourishing rather than in leading. Be like the earth: patient, broad, willing to wait. The thing to watch is passivity sliding into giving up. This week, fully support one effort someone else is leading without trying to take the wheel.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 3 – Zhun (屯) – Difficulty at the Beginning
body_md:
Zhun is thunder beneath water: clouds and thunder joined, the image of a storm as things are first born. The judgment promises great success through firm correctness, yet advises against moving in any direction for now and in favour of appointing helpers. The image teaches the noble person to bring order out of confusion as if sorting threads.

When you cast Zhun, you are in a messy beginning: no path yet, much tangled, but the seed is alive. Do not go it alone and do not force the pace. The thing to watch is losing heart and assuming you chose wrongly. This week, find one companion for what you are starting and divide the work clearly.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 4 – Meng (蒙) – Youthful Folly
body_md:
Meng is a spring issuing at the foot of a mountain: water newly risen that does not yet know its course. The judgment says learning succeeds, but it is not the teacher who seeks the pupil; asked once, the teacher answers, asked twice and three times out of doubt, the teacher falls silent. The image teaches resolute conduct and the nourishing of virtue.

When you cast Meng, you are the beginner in some field, and there is nothing shameful in that. Find someone better, ask properly and act on the answer before you doubt it. The thing to watch is asking without listening. This week, ask one person to show you a skill and practise exactly what they said at least three times.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 5 – Xu (需) – Waiting
body_md:
Xu is clouds rising to the sky: rain on its way but not yet here. The judgment says that waiting with sincerity brings brilliance and success, firm correctness brings a favourable outcome, and it is advantageous to cross the great stream. The image shows the noble person eating, drinking and enjoying themselves while they wait, as if nothing troubled them.

When you cast Xu, the moment is not ripe and your task is to wait well: not quitting, not fretting, but building strength. The thing to watch is anxious waiting that wears you down. This week, do one genuinely kind thing for yourself while you await the result you are hoping for.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 6 – Song (訟) – Conflict
body_md:
Song is heaven and water moving away from each other: the image of contention. The judgment describes someone sincere yet obstructed; a cautious halt midway turns out well, pressing to the end turns out badly; it helps to see the great person, not to cross the great stream. The image teaches the noble person to consider the beginning carefully in every undertaking.

When you cast Song, you are in or near a dispute. The ancient advice is plain: even when right, do not fight to the finish; find a trustworthy mediator. The thing to watch is an ego that wants to win. This week, in one disagreement you are having, propose a stopping point both sides can accept.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 7 – Shi (師) – The Army
body_md:
Shi is water held within the earth: strength stored and organised, like an army living among the people. The judgment says the army needs firm correctness and a leader of age and experience; then things go well and without error. The image teaches the noble person to nourish and educate the people and gather multitudes.

When you cast Shi, your situation calls for organisation, discipline and a worthy leader, whether that is you or someone you choose to follow. Strength comes from unity, not from one individual. The thing to watch is wielding authority without order. This week, clarify roles and ground rules in one group you belong to.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Hexagram 8 – Bi (比) – Holding Together
body_md:
Bi is water upon the earth: water and ground soaking into one another, the image of closeness. The judgment says holding together turns out well, but the one at the centre should examine whether they have the virtue to unite others, and the latecomer fares badly. The image recalls the ancient kings founding states and cultivating affection with the princes.

When you cast Bi, you are invited to draw nearer to people: join a group, strengthen an alliance, or become a steady point for others. The thing to watch is hesitating so long you end up outside, or bonding without sincerity. This week, reach out and arrange to meet one person you want to keep in your inner circle.
source_ref: Legge, The Yî King (1882, PD) paraphrase; editor seed 2026-10
